easy.def: A word that shows something is inside or within.
examples: The milk is in the fridge.

more.def: A word used to show that something is inside a place, a shape, a group, or a time.
examples: The fish swim in the deep part of the lake.
Our class stood in a circle.
Leaves turn red and gold in autumn.

easy.def: Not being able to do something.

more.def: The state of not being able to do something.
examples: His inability to swim kept him out of the deep water.
The team's inability to score cost them the game.
Her inability to find the keys made her late.

more.def: Impossible or very hard to reach or enter.
examples: The island was inaccessible by road.
The top shelf was inaccessible without a ladder.
The cave was inaccessible during high tide.

more.def: Not exactly right or correct.
examples: The inaccurate scale showed the wrong weight.

more.def: Not active, working or moving.
examples: The volcano has been inactive for years.
The inactive cat slept all day.

more.def: Not good enough or not enough for what is needed.
examples: The thin coat was inadequate for the cold.
The food was inadequate for so many guests.
The light was inadequate to read by.

more.def: Without meaning to; by accident.
examples: I inadvertently left my coat at school.
She inadvertently sent the message twice.
He inadvertently stepped on the cat's tail.

more.def: Not living; having no life.
examples: A rock is an inanimate object.
The toys were inanimate until the child played.

easy.def: Not right for the time or place.
examples: Shouting is inappropriate in the library.

more.def: Not suitable for the time or place, or not proper.
examples: Loud talk is inappropriate in a library.
The joke was inappropriate for school.
Wearing sandals was inappropriate for the hike.

more.def: Too quiet to be heard.
examples: The bird's song was inaudible from so far away.
The words were inaudible over the noise.

easy.def: A ceremony to start a new leader's time in office.

more.def: A special ceremony to begin a leader's time in office or the opening of something new.
examples: The president's inauguration took place in January.
Crowds came to watch the inauguration.
The inauguration of the new library was a happy event.

more.def: Too great to be counted or measured.
examples: The value of the old painting was incalculable.

more.def: Glowing brightly because of being very hot.
examples: An incandescent bulb gives off light when its wire gets hot.
The metal glowed incandescent in the fire.
The incandescent lamp lit the room.

more.def: Words that are spoken or sung to make a magic spell.
examples: The old book had an incantation to make it rain.
The baby is incapable of walking.

more.def: Not able to do something; lacking the power or skill.
examples: The baby is incapable of walking yet.
He was incapable of speaking because he was so surprised.
A fish is incapable of living on land.

easy.def: A stick or powder that smells sweet when it burns.

more.def: A substance that gives off a sweet smell when it is burned, often used in religious ceremonies.
examples: The temple smelled of sweet incense.
A stick of incense burned in a holder on the shelf.
People burn incense in many parts of the world.

easy.def: Something that makes you want to do something.

more.def: Something that makes you want to try harder, such as a reward.
examples: A prize was an incentive to read more books.
Stickers were an incentive for good behavior.
The promise of ice cream was a great incentive.

more.def: Going on and on without stopping.
examples: The incessant rain lasted all week.
The incessant noise of the traffic kept me awake.
The baby's incessant crying made it hard to sleep.

more.def: Without stopping or pausing; non-stop.
examples: It rained incessantly for three days.
He talked incessantly about the game.

easy.def: A small unit for measuring how long something is.
examples: The bug is one inch long.
The snow was an inch deep.

more.def: A small unit of length. Twelve of them make a foot.
examples: The beetle was about an inch long.
A ruler is twelve inches long.
Three inches of snow fell overnight.

easy.def: A caterpillar that moves in loops.

more.def: A small caterpillar that moves by looping its body.
examples: An inchworm crawled up the leaf.
The inchworm looped its body as it moved.
An inchworm measures a leaf by walking along it.
An odd incident happened at school.
He told us about the incident.

more.def: Something that happens, especially something unusual or surprising.
examples: A strange incident happened at lunch when the cat walked in.
The teacher wrote down the incident in her notes.
There was a small incident on the bus.

easy.def: Happening as a small extra thing.

more.def: Happening as a minor part of something else.
examples: There is an incidental cost for the bag.
The incidental music in the movie was soft.
An incidental detail did not matter.
Incidentally, I saw your friend today.
He said, "Incidentally, we have no milk."

more.def: Used to add a side comment to what you are saying.
examples: Incidentally, I saw your cousin at the store today.
We are going to the park, and, incidentally, it is a nice day.
The soup is ready and, incidentally, so is the bread.

easy.def: To burn something until nothing is left.

more.def: To burn something completely until only ashes are left.
examples: The plant incinerates the town's trash.

easy.def: A big oven that burns trash.

more.def: A large furnace for burning trash or waste.
examples: The garbage truck took the trash to the incinerator.
An incinerator burns waste at a high heat.
The school has an incinerator for old papers.

easy.def: A front tooth that cuts food.

more.def: One of the sharp front teeth used for cutting food.
examples: I lost an incisor and got a visit from the tooth fairy.
An incisor bites into an apple.

easy.def: A wish or liking to do something.
examples: I have no inclination to go.
She has an inclination to read.

more.def: A feeling that makes you want to do something.
examples: I have no inclination to go out in the rain.
She has a strong inclination to sing.
His inclination was to say yes.
The cart rolled down the incline.

more.def: A surface that slopes, like a ramp.
examples: The train slowed on the steep incline.
The road had a steep incline.
We pushed the wheelbarrow up the incline.
He is not inclined to go.

more.def: Having a wish or tendency to do something.
examples: I am inclined to say yes.
She is inclined to help whenever she can.
He is not inclined to go out in the rain.

easy.def: To make someone or something a part of a group.
examples: Please include me in your game.
We include everyone in our club.

more.def: To have as a part, or to make something part of a group.
examples: The price of the ticket includes a drink and a snack.
The tour includes a visit to the castle.
Be sure to include your name on your paper.

easy.def: Making sure everyone is part of the group.

more.def: The act of making sure that all people are part of a group and feel welcome.
examples: The school believes in the inclusion of every student.
Inclusion means everyone gets a turn.

more.def: Including everyone and treating all people fairly.
examples: Our club is inclusive, so everyone can join.
The playground is inclusive for all kids.
An inclusive team welcomes every player.

easy.def: In disguise so no one knows you.

more.def: With your real name or identity hidden.
examples: The prince traveled incognito through the village.
She went to the party incognito.
He walked incognito in a hat and glasses.
The family has a good income.

more.def: The money that a person or family receives, usually from work.
examples: Her income from the farm rose this year.
The family had a small income.
The incoming mail is on the desk.

more.def: Coming in or arriving.
examples: The incoming tide covered the sand.
An incoming call rang on the phone.
The incoming class has thirty students.

more.def: So good that nothing can be compared to it.
examples: The mountain offered an incomparable view.
He had an incomparable talent for art.

easy.def: Not being able to do a job well.

more.def: Lack of skill or ability to do a job properly.
examples: The incompetence of the worker was clear.

easy.def: Not able to do a job well.

more.def: Not having the skill or ability to do something well.
examples: The incompetent worker kept making mistakes.
He felt incompetent when he could not fix the bike.
The incompetent guide got us lost.

more.def: Not finished, or missing some parts.
examples: The puzzle was incomplete because one piece was missing.
Her homework was incomplete, so she finished it after dinner.
The list of names is incomplete.

more.def: Impossible to understand.
examples: The directions were so messy they were incomprehensible.
The foreign sign was incomprehensible to us.

more.def: Impossible to imagine or believe.
examples: It is inconceivable that the sun would not rise.
The size of space is almost inconceivable.
It was inconceivable to him that he could lose.

easy.def: Not thinking about how others feel.
examples: It is inconsiderate to be loud at night.
He was inconsiderate and took all the cake.

more.def: Not caring about the feelings or needs of other people.
examples: It was inconsiderate to play loud music while the baby slept.
The inconsiderate boy left his mess for others to clean.
She felt bad for being inconsiderate to her friend.

more.def: Not staying the same, or not matching other things.
examples: The inconsistent weather went from sunny to rainy.
Her answers were inconsistent, so we were not sure.
The team was inconsistent and won only some games.

easy.def: So sad you cannot be comforted.

more.def: So sad that nothing can comfort you.
examples: The child was inconsolable when her toy broke.
The puppy howled, inconsolable, when left alone.
She was inconsolable after her friend moved.

more.def: Not easy to notice or see.
examples: The gray mouse was inconspicuous against the floor.
She found an inconspicuous seat at the back.
The plain bird was inconspicuous in the brown bush.
I am sorry for the inconvenience.

more.def: Something that causes a little trouble or makes things harder.
examples: The late bus was an inconvenience.
The detour was a minor inconvenience.
The closed road caused some inconvenience.

more.def: Causing trouble or making things harder, because it is not handy or does not suit you.
examples: The bus stop is inconvenient because it is far from my house.
It was an inconvenient time for a phone call.
The long walk was inconvenient with heavy bags.

easy.def: To include something as part of a whole.

more.def: To include something as a part of a larger whole.
examples: The chef incorporated fresh herbs into the sauce.
We incorporated your idea into the plan.
The design incorporates a small garden.

more.def: Not correct, or not matching the facts or the rules.
examples: My answer on the math test was incorrect, so I fixed it.
The spelling of the word is incorrect.
The teacher showed us that our idea was incorrect.

more.def: In a way that is wrong or not right.
To become larger or to make something larger in amount or number.
examples: The price of milk will increase next month.
The plant increased in height every week.
She increased the volume on the radio.
There was an increase in price.

more.def: A rise in size, amount or number.
examples: There was an increase in the price of gas.
The increase in snow made the roads slippery.
We saw an increase in visitors.

easy.def: More and more as time goes on.

more.def: More and more as time goes on.
examples: The path became increasingly steep as we climbed.
As the storm came closer, the sky grew increasingly dark.
She felt increasingly confident each time she practiced.

more.def: So amazing or surprising that it is hard to believe.
examples: The view from the mountain was incredible.
The magician did an incredible trick.

more.def: To a very great degree, in a way that is hard to believe.
examples: It was incredibly cold last night.

more.def: Not willing or able to believe something, because it seems too strange.
examples: She gave an incredulous look when he said he had seen a dragon.
He was incredulous when he heard the news.
The class stared at the teacher, incredulous.

easy.def: Keeping eggs warm so they hatch.

more.def: The act of keeping eggs warm until the babies hatch.
examples: The incubation of the eggs took three weeks.
The hen sat on the eggs during incubation.

easy.def: A warm box for hatching eggs or helping tiny babies.
examples: The eggs are in an incubator.
A baby chick came from the incubator.

more.def: A warm, safe box used to hatch eggs or to keep very small, early babies warm.
examples: The chicks hatched in the incubator.
A tiny baby was kept warm in an incubator.
The eggs stayed in the incubator for three weeks.

more.def: Owing thanks or money to someone.
examples: I am indebted to you for your help.
She felt indebted to her teacher.
The town is indebted to the firefighters.

more.def: The state of being unable to make up your mind.
examples: His indecision about which toy to buy took a long time.
She stood in indecision at the door.

more.def: Used to show that something is really true.
examples: It was indeed the best day of my life.
Yes, indeed, we are ready to go.

easy.def: For an unknown length of time.

more.def: For a time that has no set end.

easy.def: To start a line a little way in from the edge.

more.def: To start a line of writing a little way in from the edge of the page.
examples: Remember to indent each new paragraph.
She indented the first line of her story.
The teacher showed us how to indent.

easy.def: A small dip in a surface.
examples: There is an indentation in the pillow.

more.def: A dent, notch or dip in a surface, or the blank space at the start of a line of writing.
examples: There was an indentation in the sand where she sat.
Start each paragraph with an indentation.
The chair left an indentation in the carpet.

easy.def: Being free and able to do things yourself.

more.def: The freedom to make your own choices and do things without help, or the freedom of a country to rule itself.
examples: She is learning independence by making her own lunch.
The country celebrated its independence with a parade.
A bike gave him the independence to ride to school by himself.
The independent boy tied his shoes.

more.def: Able to do things on your own, without help from others.
examples: I am independent now and tie my own shoes.
The country became independent after many years.

easy.def: Too great to put into words.

more.def: So great or strange that it cannot be put into words.
examples: The view from the top was indescribable.

easy.def: Not able to be broken or ruined.
examples: He thought his fort was indestructible.
A hero in the comic is indestructible.

more.def: Impossible to destroy, break or wear out.
examples: The superhero in the cartoon has an indestructible shield.
No toy is truly indestructible, even the strongest ones.
The scientists tested a nearly indestructible new plastic.

easy.def: A list at the back of a book that tells where to find things.

more.def: An alphabetical list at the back of a book that tells you which pages to find things on.
examples: I looked up "volcano" in the index to find the right page.
The index of the book listed every animal in order.
Use the index to find the topic you need.

easy.def: To show or point to something.
examples: The light indicates that it is ready.

more.def: To show or point out something, or to be a sign of it.
examples: The arrow on the sign indicates which way to go.
Dark clouds indicate that rain may fall.
The light on the oven indicates that it is hot.
Smoke is an indication of fire.
There was no indication of the cat.

more.def: A sign or hint that shows what is happening or will happen.
examples: Dark clouds are an indication of rain.
There was no indication that anyone had been in the room.
The red light is an indication that the oven is hot.

easy.def: Something that shows you what is happening.

more.def: A thing, such as a light or a dial, that shows what is going on.
examples: The fuel indicator showed the tank was nearly empty.
A red light is an indicator that the oven is on.
A rising temperature is an indicator of fever.
She greeted the news with indifference.

more.def: A lack of interest or concern.
examples: He shrugged with indifference when asked to choose.
The cat looked at the toy with indifference.
The class received the news with indifference.
He was indifferent to the game.

more.def: Not interested in something or not caring which happens.
examples: He seemed indifferent to the game and read a book.
The cat was indifferent to the new toy.
She was indifferent about which movie to see.

easy.def: In a way that shows you do not care.

more.def: In a way that shows you do not care much.
examples: The cat watched the dog indifferently.

easy.def: Living in a place from the very beginning.

more.def: Belonging to a place from the earliest times, such as the first people or the plants and animals that began there.
examples: The kangaroo is indigenous to Australia.
Indigenous peoples were the first to live on these lands.
The indigenous plants of the desert need little water.
Too much pizza gave me indigestion.

more.def: A sore or uncomfortable feeling in the stomach, caused by eating too much or too fast.
examples: I got indigestion from eating too much pizza.
He has indigestion when he eats too quickly.

easy.def: Angry because something is not fair.

more.def: Angry because you feel that you have been treated unfairly.
examples: She was indignant when they said she had cheated.
He gave an indignant cry when his turn was skipped.
The indignant cat hissed when it was put in the bath.

easy.def: Anger when something is not fair.

more.def: Strong anger that you feel when something seems unfair.
examples: He felt indignation when someone cut in line.
She spoke with indignation after being blamed.
The crowd shouted with indignation at the decision.

more.def: A deep blue color with a hint of purple, one of the colors of the rainbow.
examples: Indigo is the color between blue and violet in the rainbow.
The sky turned a deep indigo as night fell.

more.def: Not going straight to the point, place or person.
examples: We took an indirect route that curved around the lake.

easy.def: So important you cannot do without it.

more.def: So important or useful that you cannot do without it.
examples: A map is indispensable on a hike.

more.def: Not clear or easy to see, hear or tell apart.
examples: An indistinct shape moved in the fog.
The voices were indistinct from far away.
The writing on the old sign was indistinct.

easy.def: So alike you cannot tell apart.

more.def: So similar that you cannot tell them apart.
examples: The copy was indistinguishable from the original.
Each individual cup has a lid.

more.def: Single and separate from others, or meant for one person.
examples: Each child got an individual cup of juice.
The teacher gave individual help to each student.
Each snowflake has an individual shape.
An individual can make a difference.

more.def: One single person, as different from a group.
examples: Every individual has a different fingerprint.
One individual can make a difference.
She is a kind and thoughtful individual.

easy.def: What makes you different from everyone else.

more.def: The qualities that make a person different from everyone else.
examples: She shows her individuality through her clothes.
Each artist's individuality shows in the paintings.
Our teacher likes to see individuality in our writing.

more.def: Separately, one by one.
examples: The teacher spoke to the students individually.

more.def: Not able to be divided or split into parts.
examples: The team felt like an indivisible unit.
The pieces formed an indivisible whole.
We play indoor games on a rainy day.

more.def: Done or found inside a building.
examples: An indoor pool lets us swim all winter.
Rain meant we played indoor games all afternoon.
The indoor plants need light from the window.

more.def: Inside a building or house, not outside.
examples: We stayed indoors because of the thunderstorm.
The children played board games indoors on the rainy day.
Please come indoors and wash your hands.

more.def: To cause something to happen, or to persuade someone to do something.
examples: Nothing could induce him to go near the dog.

easy.def: To let yourself have something special.

more.def: To let yourself or someone else have what they enjoy, especially more than is good.
examples: We indulged in a big slice of cake.
Grandpa likes to indulge the grandchildren with treats.
She indulged herself with an extra hour of reading.
The ice cream was an indulgence.

more.def: Something that you enjoy and do not really need, or giving in to what someone wants.
examples: A big piece of cake was a sweet indulgence.
The grandparents' indulgence made the kids happy.
Chocolate is an indulgence for many people.

easy.def: Too kind and ready to give people what they want.

more.def: Kind and willing to let someone have what they want, even too much.
examples: Her indulgent grandfather gave her extra candy.
The indulgent parent let the kids stay up late.
An indulgent smile spread over her face.

easy.def: Having to do with factories and big businesses.
examples: The industrial part of town has big factories.

more.def: Having to do with factories and making things in large amounts.
examples: The industrial area of the city is full of factories and warehouses.
The industrial revolution brought machines into many workplaces.
A large industrial fan kept the factory cool.

more.def: Hard-working and busy.
examples: The industrious ants carried food to their nest.
She is an industrious student who finishes her work.
The industrious beavers built a dam.

easy.def: All the businesses that make one kind of thing.

more.def: All the companies and work that make a certain kind of thing or give a certain service.
examples: The car industry builds millions of cars each year.
Tourism is a big industry in the town.

easy.def: Not safe or fit to eat.

more.def: Not safe or good to eat.
examples: The berries on that bush are inedible.

more.def: Not working or not having the result that you want.
examples: The ineffective plan did not help.
The ineffective cleaner left the stain.

more.def: Wasting time, effort or energy and not getting good results.
examples: Carrying water in a spoon is inefficient.
The inefficient worker took all day.
It was inefficient to walk all the way back.

easy.def: When things are not the same or fair.
examples: There was inequality in the game.

more.def: A lack of equal treatment, share or size among people or things.
examples: The children talked about inequality in how toys were shared.
There was inequality in the sizes of the pieces.
The class discussed fairness and inequality.

more.def: Not moving, or not reacting with other things.
examples: The inert body lay on the sand.

easy.def: The tendency to keep doing what you are doing.

more.def: The tendency of an object to keep still or keep moving unless a force acts on it.
examples: Inertia keeps a rolling ball moving.
It takes force to overcome inertia.
Inertia pushes you forward when the bus stops.

more.def: Impossible to avoid or get away from.
examples: The smell of the skunk was inescapable.
It was an inescapable fact that winter was coming.

more.def: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid.
examples: Rain was inevitable in the spring.
Change is inevitable as we grow up.
With the clouds above, a storm was inevitable.

easy.def: So bad it cannot be forgiven.

more.def: Too bad to be excused or forgiven.
examples: Being late without calling was inexcusable.
It is inexcusable to be rude to guests.
The inexcusable mistake cost us the game.

more.def: Never running out; impossible to use up.
examples: The kids seemed to have inexhaustible energy.
The spring gave an inexhaustible supply of water.

more.def: Not costing much money.
examples: The toy was inexpensive, so I bought two.
They sell inexpensive notebooks at the store.
Walking is an inexpensive way to travel.

more.def: Having little experience or skill because you are new to something.
examples: The class had an inexperienced teacher.

more.def: Impossible to explain or understand.
examples: The sudden noise in the night was inexplicable.
It was inexplicable how the keys ended up on the roof.

easy.def: Too big to put into words.

more.def: Too strong or great to be put into words.
examples: The view was one of inexpressible beauty.

more.def: Well known for something bad or wrong, not for something good.
examples: The infamous pirate was known for stealing treasure from many ships.
The old road is infamous for its sharp, dangerous curves.
The fox was infamous in the village for stealing eggs.

easy.def: The time when you are a baby.

more.def: The very early time of life when you are a baby.
examples: The town was still in its infancy.

more.def: A baby in its first year of life.
examples: The infant slept in her mother's arms.
An infant needs a lot of care.
The nurse held the tiny infant.

more.def: Soldiers who move and fight on foot.
examples: The infantry marched through the valley.
In the old days, the infantry walked while the cavalry rode.

easy.def: To make someone sick with germs.

more.def: To pass germs to a person, animal or plant so that it becomes sick.
examples: The cut became infected, and the doctor gave her medicine.

more.def: A sickness that is caused by germs entering the body.
examples: I had an ear infection and took medicine.
Washing your hands helps stop infection.

more.def: Able to spread easily from one person to another, like a sickness or a feeling.
examples: The flu is infectious, so stay home when you have it.
Her laugh was so infectious that everyone joined in.

easy.def: To figure something out from clues.

more.def: To figure something out from clues instead of being told.
examples: I infer from the wet ground that it rained.
She inferred the answer from clues.
What can you infer about the character?

easy.def: A guess you make from clues.

more.def: A conclusion you reach from clues or facts.
examples: From the muddy boots, I made an inference that it had rained.
Good readers make inferences while they read.
Her inference turned out to be right.
This toy is inferior to that one.

more.def: Lower in quality, rank or value than something else.
examples: The cheap pen was inferior to the one I had before, and it leaked.
Nobody should be made to feel inferior to another person.
The inferior boots let in water on the very first day.

more.def: A huge, fierce fire that burns out of control.
examples: Firefighters battled the inferno in the forest.
The barn became an inferno in minutes.
Smoke rose from the raging inferno.

easy.def: To fill a place with bugs or pests.
examples: Rats can infest an old barn.

more.def: To be in a place in large numbers and cause trouble, as insects or pests do.
examples: Termites infested the old wooden fence.
Weeds can infest a garden if they are not pulled.

easy.def: When too many bugs are in one place.
examples: There was an infestation of ants.

more.def: A large number of pests, such as insects, in a place where they cause harm.
examples: The garden had an infestation of aphids.
There was an infestation of ants in the kitchen.
An infestation of mice was found in the barn.

easy.def: The inner part of a baseball field.
examples: The player ran in the infield.
The ball rolled in the infield.

more.def: The part of a baseball field inside the bases.
examples: The ball rolled across the infield.
The infield grass is cut short.
The shortstop plays in the infield.

more.def: Having no end or limit.
examples: Some people believe that space is infinite.
She had infinite patience with the little children.

easy.def: So small you can hardly see.

more.def: Extremely small, almost too small to measure.
examples: An infinitesimal speck of dust floated by.
She added an infinitesimal amount of salt.

easy.def: A number or space that never ends.

more.def: Endless space, time or number that has no limit.
examples: The stars seem to stretch to infinity.
You can count numbers all day and never reach infinity.
The symbol for infinity looks like a figure eight on its side.

easy.def: A place at a school where sick people are cared for.
examples: The nurse is in the infirmary.

more.def: A place in a school or large building where sick or hurt people are cared for.
examples: She went to the school infirmary when she had a fever.
The nurse put a bandage on him in the infirmary.
The infirmary has beds and medicine.

more.def: Easily set on fire; flammable.
examples: Keep inflammable things away from the fire.
The inflammable cloth caught fire quickly.

easy.def: Able to be filled with air.

more.def: Able to be filled with air so that it gets big.
examples: We rode in an inflatable boat.
The inflatable pool filled with water.
An inflatable toy floated on the lake.

more.def: To fill something with air or gas so it gets bigger.
examples: Dad inflated the bike tire with a pump.
She inflated the balloon for the party.
He inflated the raft before the trip.

easy.def: Filled with air, or too high.

more.def: Filled with air or gas, or made larger than it should be.
examples: The price was inflated for the holiday.
An inflated raft floated on the lake.

easy.def: The rise and fall of your voice.

more.def: A change in the pitch or tone of the voice as you speak.
examples: She read with lots of inflection.
The rise in his inflection showed he was asking a question.
A flat voice with no inflection is dull.

easy.def: To make someone suffer or put up with something unpleasant.

more.def: To cause something harmful or unpleasant to happen to someone.
examples: The storm inflicted damage on the town.
It is wrong to inflict pain on any animal.
The long, boring talk inflicted misery on the audience.

easy.def: The power to change someone or something.
examples: Friends have an influence on us.
The moon has an influence on the tides.
Her teacher was a good influence.

more.def: The power to change how someone thinks or acts, or to change how something happens.
